correctness.rationale: For product xy=B(x,y)u, any algebra endomorphism T has T(u)=c u and B(Tx,Ty)=c B(x,y). For rank one and nonsingular n>=3 form, c=0 by rank comparison, so T(u)=0 and its rank-one image is B-singular; conversely these conditions suffice for multiplicativity. Such composition-idempotents are exactly (isotropic image line ell, complementary kernel hyperplane H containing u), with q^(n-2) choices per ell != Ku. Two distinct rank-one projections commute only when both products vanish, i.e. each line lies in the other kernel. The fiber over ell,m has q^(2n-6) edges when u is outside ell+m and zero otherwise. If u is anisotropic, a secant-plane root involution counts (M-S)/2 forbidden pairs; if u is isotropic, every quotient-singular line contributes one totally singular plane carrying q allowed lines, for q(q-1)J/2 forbidden pairs. Standard Witt decomposition gives exact singular-line formulas for even/odd spaces and a 2q^(s-1) hyperplane-line difference between the two anisotropic norm classes in ambient odd dimension 2s+1. This gives the sharp edge gap q^(2n-6+s-1). Independently built normalized isotropic lines over F3^3, enumerated rank-one projections and literal matrix compositions; verified (V,E)=(12,4),(12,5),(9,3) for u=(1,0,0),(1,1,0),(1,1,1). This is a finite corroboration of a complete symbolic proof, not an all-field enumeration.
